title: Three alternatives, four criteria (variant II of the SAW/COPRAS comparison)

source.citation: Podvezko, V. (2011). The comparative analysis of MCDA methods SAW and COPRAS. Inzinerine Ekonomika - Engineering Economics, 22(2), 134-146.
source.note: Open-access paper from the method's school (Vilnius Gediminas Technical University). The original COPRAS paper (Zavadskas, Kaklauskas, Sarka 1994, Technological and Economic Development of Economy 1(3), 131-139) is not available online; see docs/methods/copras.md.

sPlus.printedIn: Table 8, COPRAS row S+j, variant II

sMinus.printedIn: Table 8, COPRAS row S-j, variant II

relativeSignificance.printedIn: Table 8, COPRAS row Zj, variant II

ranking.printedIn: Table 8, COPRAS row Rank, variant II

notes: Normalisation is by the column sum, d_ij = w_j x_ij / sum_i x_ij, for both benefit and cost criteria (Eq. 6). S+ and S- sum the weighted values of the benefit and cost criteria.

Relative significance Q_j = S+_j + sum S- / (S-_j * sum (1 / S-)) (Eq. 11), the form with S-_min cancelled; Zavadskas et al. write it with S-_min (Eq. 8), which is algebraically identical. Utility degree N_j = 100 Q_j / max Q (not printed in this paper).

Variant I (x_41 = 105, x_42 = 215) is not used: the Z row printed for it repeats the variant II values, while its own S- and ranks (1, 3, 2) correspond to Z = 0.336, 0.328, 0.336. That is a printing error in Table 8.
The example shows COPRAS rank reversal under a small data change: variant I ranks A1 first, variant II ranks A3 first.
